test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a cause of high oil pressure in the lubrication system of an engine?
solution:
The correct answer is __High oil viscosity__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• High oil viscosity__ is one of the significant causes of high oil pressure in an engine's lubrication system.
 
• Oil viscosity refers to the thickness or resistance to flow of the oil.
 
• When the oil viscosity is too high, it becomes difficult for the oil to flow through the lubrication system, resulting in increased pressure.
 
• This can occur due to using oil with incorrect specifications or in extremely cold temperatures where the oil thickens.
 
• It is essential to use the manufacturer-recommended oil grade for optimal engine performance.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Low oil level:**

 
 
• A low oil level does not cause high oil pressure; instead, it can result in inadequate lubrication and potential engine damage.
 
 
 
• **External oil leakage:**
 
 
• External oil leakage does not increase oil pressure; it results in loss of oil from the system.
 
 
 
• **Oil pump gear wear:**
 
 
• Worn oil pump gears usually lead to low oil pressure, not high oil pressure.
